summary.intent: Implement a delegated-ipfs.dev fallback for IPNS routing in the DelegatedRoutingClient, with Prometheus metrics to expose fallback frequency in Grafana.
summary.outcome: Fallback logic was implemented at the API level in DelegatedRoutingClient with Prometheus counters tracking primary vs fallback backend usage. All 27 client tests and 58 IPNS service tests pass; changes were committed and pushed.

repo: Someguy's SOMEGUY_IPNS_ENDPOINTS does concurrent fanout (race), not sequential fallback — it queries DHT and delegated endpoint in parallel and returns the winner, with no per-source metrics exposure.
Fallback routing must be implemented at the API layer (DelegatedRoutingClient) rather than someguy config to get meaningful observability.
MetricsService is the central place to register Prometheus counters; DelegatedRoutingClient is injected via DelegatedRoutingModule.
Jest must be run from the api directory or with a specific config path — running from repo root requires different invocation.

code.finding: Rewritten to add fallback to delegated-ipfs.dev when someguy fails after retries, with {backend='primary'|'fallback'} label on Prometheus counters.
New counters added for delegated routing backend hits (primary/fallback/error).
Test suite expanded to 27 tests covering fallback behavior and metric counter assertions.
Updated to document/pass the fallback URL env var for staging deployments.

workflow: Research agent was used to investigate existing metrics setup before writing new metric definitions — avoids duplication.
Running tests in three scopes (client spec, ipns service spec, republish spec) validated no regressions across all consumers of DelegatedRoutingClient.
Jest invocation from repo root vs api directory has different behavior — prefer running from the app directory directly.

friction: Jest test runner location confusion — required multiple attempts (checking jest config, finding spec file, running from different directories) before finding the correct invocation.
Initial design considered someguy-level SOMEGUY_IPNS_ENDPOINTS config before discovering it performs concurrent fanout rather than fallback, requiring a design pivot.
open_items: Grafana dashboard configuration for the new fallback metrics counters was not set up — metrics are being emitted but no dashboard panels were created to visualize fallback frequency.
Untracked load test metrics JSON files and .env restoration were left out of the PR intentionally — may need cleanup or gitignore entries.
The someguy-level SOMEGUY_IPNS_ENDPOINTS fanout behavior could be useful for latency optimization in the future, separate from fallback concerns.
